settings.kill_roas_threshold: pause if ROAS < 1.0x after ₹500 spend on a sales-objective campaign
settings.reactivate_min_historic_roas: surface for reactivation if a paused campaign's last active-period ROAS >= 3.0x
settings.budget_reallocation_min_roas_gap: shift budget when one active campaign's ROAS is 1.5x+ another's
settings.note: hard_spend_ceiling_inr is a placeholder — set to roughly 3x trailing-30-day avg daily spend (~₹663/day as of 29 Aug 2026). All fields here are editable directly in the Automation tab (Save button) or by telling Claude.

proposals.title: Reactivate Kage_Sales
proposals.reasoning: Kage_Sales is currently paused but was the best-volume winner in the account: 4.30x ROAS on ₹6,195 spend and 10 purchases over its last active 30-day window — well above every other campaign, active or paused, and above the 3.0x reactivation threshold.
proposals.actionSummary: Reactivate campaign 'Kage_Sales' (id 120255012429830159) with a conservative starting daily budget (≈₹200–300/day, versus its historical pace) and monitor for 3 days before scaling further.

params.note: set an explicit conservative daily budget before or immediately after activation

proposals.title: Launch a retargeting campaign against 30d add-to-cart non-purchasers
proposals.reasoning: Account-level 30d data: 83 add-to-cart events vs 15 purchases — roughly 68 people added to cart in the last 30 days without completing a purchase. Refreshed pixel-level check on 2026-08-29 (trailing 7d window) shows the same pattern continuing: ~50 AddToCart events vs 11 Purchases. No retargeting campaign currently exists against this group.
proposals.actionSummary: Create a custom audience of site visitors who added to cart or initiated checkout in the last 14 days without purchasing (pixel-based), then launch a small retargeting campaign using the Kage_Sales creative (highest historical ROAS in the account, 4.30x).

params.name: ATC/Checkout - No Purchase 14d
params.rule_note: add_to_cart OR initiate_checkout events, excluding purchase event

params.note: pair with ads_create_ad_set targeting the new custom audience and ads_create_ad reusing the Kage_Sales creative

proposals.title: Launch a Dynamic Product Ads (DPA) campaign from the connected Shopify catalog
proposals.reasoning: A Shopify product catalog is already connected to this ad account (catalog_id 1149969713295773), but zero DPA/catalog-based campaigns are currently running. Gully Labs (main competitor) runs DCO/catalog ads as part of their active mix; KAI runs none. This is a structural gap, not a performance one. Meta's own Opportunity Score tool (account score 85/100 as of 2026-08-29, down from 88) still flags Advantage+ catalog ads as a top recommendation (+4 points, 'lower cost per action'). Catalog health check re-run on 2026-08-29 found the same 3 diagnostic issues, one improved: 18 items still marked out-of-stock (must_fix — these won't appear in dynamic ads, unchanged), 24 items with fewer than 2 images (opportunity, unchanged), and only 1 unmatched content ID between the catalog and pixel now (opportunity, down from 4).
proposals.actionSummary: Fix the 18 out-of-stock catalog items first (update availability), check catalog health (ads_catalog_get_diagnostics), create a product set for best-sellers, and launch a catalog sales (DPA) campaign targeting site visitors/past purchasers.

params.note: start with a best-sellers product set before a full-catalog campaign; confirm out-of-stock items are resolved first
catalog-based dynamic ad against the new product set

proposals.title: Exclude existing purchasers from Kage_sales_1908 prospecting targeting
proposals.reasoning: Kage_sales_1908 is the account's only active sales-objective prospecting campaign (₹5,089.63 spent in the last 30 days, ROAS 1.57x — down from 1.84x on 2026-08-28's smaller spend base). Its ad set (id 120255351569140159) targets broad interest/behavior segments (Footwear, Sneakers, Street fashion, Frequent Travelers, Engaged Shoppers) with Advantage+ audience expansion on, but the targeting spec still has no excluded_custom_audiences entry — re-checked directly against the live targeting spec on 2026-08-29. A re-check of the account's custom audiences on 2026-08-29 found an existing 'Purchasers 30D' audience (id 120249907176770159, subtype PLATFORM/website pixel-based, delivery_status ACTIVE) that was not previously known — no need to create a new audience, it can be applied directly. Some fraction of prospecting spend is likely re-reaching people who already bought, which understates true new-customer efficiency.
proposals.actionSummary: Add the existing 'Purchasers 30D' custom audience (id 120249907176770159) as an excluded audience on Kage_sales_1908's ad set targeting, leaving all other targeting unchanged. No new audience needs to be created.

params.note: add existing custom audience id 120249907176770159 ('Purchasers 30D') to excluded_custom_audiences in the existing targeting spec; do not otherwise modify targeting

proposals.title: Exclude WhatsApp placement from Kage_sales_1908
proposals.reasoning: 30d placement breakdown for Kage_sales_1908 (the account's only active sales campaign): the 'whatsapp_marketing_messages' placement spent ₹262.34 on 195 impressions with 0 attributed purchases, at a CPM of ₹1,345.33 — roughly 11x the campaign's android_smartphone CPM (₹117.96) and 8x its iPhone CPM (₹160.51). This same spend shows up identically in the device breakdown as the 'other' impression_device bucket (₹262.34, CPM ₹1,345.33, 0 purchases) — same underlying placement, two views of the same number, not a separate issue. ₹262.34 is ~5.2% of the campaign's ₹5,089.64 30d spend going to a placement with zero conversions at a wildly elevated CPM. By contrast, this campaign's two dominant placements — instagram_reels (₹2,217.98, 1 purchase, 1.13x ROAS) and instagram_stories (₹780.12, 2 purchases, 7.01x ROAS) — are both converting, so this isn't a whole-campaign problem, just this one placement.
proposals.actionSummary: Remove 'whatsapp' from Kage_sales_1908's ad set targeting.publisher_platforms (keep facebook, instagram, audience_network, threads as-is). Note: Meta's targeting spec is inclusion-based (no separate excluded_publisher_platforms field), so this is applied by narrowing the publisher_platforms list rather than adding an exclusion.

params.note: remove 'whatsapp' from the existing targeting.publisher_platforms list; leave every other targeting parameter (including the purchaser exclusion from A-004, if already applied) unchanged

proposals.title: Shift Kage_sales_1908 budget weight from 25-34 male toward 35-44 male
proposals.reasoning: 30d age/gender breakdown for Kage_sales_1908 (the account's only active sales campaign): the 25-34 male cell spent ₹2,408.32 (the single largest demo allocation in the campaign) for 1 purchase, ROAS 1.11x — below the campaign's own 30d blended ROAS (1.57x) and well below account average. The 35-44 male cell spent ₹1,118.80, less than half as much, but returned 2 purchases at 4.74x ROAS — over 4x more efficient per rupee spent. Both cells clear a ₹500+ meaningful-spend bar. 18-24 male (₹694.96, 0 purchases) is also underperforming. This is a real, spend-backed efficiency gap within one active campaign, not a cross-objective comparison.
proposals.actionSummary: Reduce budget weight/targeting emphasis on the 25-34 male age-gender cell and increase it on 35-44 male within Kage_sales_1908's ad set targeting. Suggest tightening age_max toward 44 or applying an Advantage+ audience budget skew if available, rather than a hard age cutoff, since sample size (3 total purchases) is still thin.

params.note: adjust age range / demo weighting to favor 35-44 male over 25-34 male based on 30d ROAS gap (4.74x vs 1.11x); sample is thin (3 purchases total) so treat as a lean, not a hard cutoff

proposals.title: Refresh the stale purchase-based lookalike audience
proposals.reasoning: The account's only active purchase-based lookalike ('Lookalike (1%) - Shopify Meta Pixel - Website using Purchase', id 120250736441810159, subtype LOOKALIKE, delivery_status ACTIVE) was created 2026-05-27 — 94 days old as of 2026-08-29, well past the 14-day lookalike_refresh_days threshold. No 2%/5% variants exist at all. Note: the 'Purchasers 30D' PLATFORM custom audience (id 120249907176770159, used in A-004) only shows an approximate matched size of ~20 users — too small to be a reliable independent LAL source on its own; the existing pixel-purchase-event LAL is the better-matched source and is the one that needs refreshing, not a new build from 'Purchasers 30D'.
proposals.actionSummary: Rebuild the 1% purchase-based lookalike off current pixel purchase-event data (refresh, same source definition), and create matching 2% and 5% variants that don't currently exist, so retargeting/prospecting campaigns have a size ladder to test against.

params.name: Lookalike (IN, 1%) - Purchase Pixel - Refresh 2026-08-29
params.note: rebuild off the same Shopify/Meta Pixel purchase-event source as audience 120250736441810159; also create 2% and 5% variants

As of 2026-08-29: frequency (1.04, trailing 7d) is still healthy, no fatigue. CTR has softened to 1.65% (trailing 7d) from 2.20% previously — worth watching but not yet a trigger on its own. Flagging so it stays on your radar if it doesn't start feeding a retargeting/conversion campaign soon.

alerts.title: 126 total campaigns on the account, 2 active
alerts.detail: The account has a long tail of old paused/dead campaigns (Black Friday, Diwali, and other one-off pushes going back over a year). Not urgent, but worth an archive/cleanup pass — a fragmented account history makes some of Meta's own learning-phase and benchmark signals less reliable.

alerts.title: Geo scaling/suppression can't run yet — Meta doesn't return purchase attribution at region level
alerts.detail: Checked the 30d region breakdown for both active campaigns. Kage_sales_1908 (the only sales campaign) has real spend concentration — Maharashtra ₹1,985.20 (2.16% CTR), Karnataka ₹902.39 (2.33% CTR), Telangana ₹584.60, Delhi ₹543.81 — but every single region row came back with omni_purchase/purchase_roas = null. This isn't a spend-volume problem (Maharashtra alone clears any reasonable meaningful-spend bar); it's the same Meta API limitation already disclosed on the dashboard's Geography tab (purchase attribution isn't returned cross-tabbed with region breakdowns). geo-scaling, geo-suppression, and new-geo-testing can only run on a CTR proxy until that changes, so skipped this run rather than propose budget moves off a proxy metric alone. Re-evaluate once spend is high enough to justify the same CTR-relative-ROAS estimation methodology the dashboard already uses for this tab.

alerts.title: Account-wide hourly pattern: 00:00-13:59 converts ~2.3x more efficiently than 14:00-23:59
alerts.detail: 30d hourly breakdown (advertiser timezone), account-wide: the 00:00-13:59 window spent ₹8,813.10 for 10 purchases (~₹881/purchase); the 14:00-23:59 window spent ₹9,935.47 for only 5 purchases (~₹1,987/purchase) — comparable spend, roughly half the conversion efficiency. Caveat: this pull is account-wide, not isolated to Kage_sales_1908 (the only sales campaign) — Kage_TOF (traffic-only, always 0 purchases) shares the same hourly spend pattern and could be diluting the read. Not filing a dayparting schedule-change proposal off a mixed-campaign signal; recommend a Kage_sales_1908-only hourly pull to confirm before acting.

alerts.title: Kage_TOF: CTR down 38% week-over-week, not frequency-driven
alerts.detail: Kage_TOF's single active ad: CTR dropped from 2.35% (16-22 Aug) to 1.45% (23-29 Aug) — a 38.3% week-over-week decline, crossing the 30% creative-fatigue trigger — while spend rose (₹840.76 → ₹945.47) and frequency stayed flat (1.071 → 1.077, so this isn't frequency/audience-saturation driven, more likely creative wear-out or an auction/algorithm shift). Not filed as an executable proposal: there's no ready replacement creative to rotate in yet (that needs the Phase 3 auto-creative-generation pipeline, not yet built). Recommend a manual creative refresh review for this ad in the meantime.

alerts.title: Dashboard's static 30d snapshot is 2 days stale but reconciles correctly
alerts.detail: Dashboard shows a 30d snapshot dated 'Jul 29-Aug 27': ₹17,258 spend, ₹36,129 revenue, 15 purchases, 2.09x ROAS. Fresh pull today (30d window now Jul 31-Aug 29): ₹18,748.59 spend, ~₹36,126 revenue, 15 purchases, ~1.93x ROAS. Purchases and revenue are unchanged (matches the day-wise Aug 27-29 data showing 0 new purchases those days) — the spend/ROAS difference is fully explained by the 30d window rolling forward 2 days (higher-spend late-July days dropped off, replaced by Aug 28-29), not a data or pipeline error. Recommend refreshing the baked-in dashboard snapshot on the next content session so the displayed window stays current.

alerts.title: Week of Aug 23-29: automation build week, spend steady, ROAS soft
alerts.detail: This week: both active campaigns combined spent roughly ₹4,517 (Kage_sales_1908 ₹3,571.52 + Kage_TOF ₹945.47, 23-29 Aug ad-level). Kage_sales_1908 CTR held at 2.12% (vs 2.11% prior week); Kage_TOF CTR fell 38% (see AL-006). On the automation side: shipped the in-app parameter/targeting editor (audience, geo, interests, behaviors, devices, placements, all real dropdowns/search, pre-filled from live targeting), extended the in-app dispatcher to cover creative uploads and A/B test creation, and ran a full module pass adding A-005 through A-007 and this batch of alerts. Three proposals (A-001, A-002, A-003) plus the two new ones (A-006, A-007) remain pending approval.
